column1: zsh: give a directory a short name usable ANYWHERE a path is (not just cd)?
column2:
hash -d notes=~/notes      # define: name -> path
cd ~notes                  # jump there
nvim ~notes/todo.md        # works mid-path, tab-completes, prompt shows ~notes

Put the `hash -d` lines in .zshrc (ordering vs p10k instant-prompt doesn't
matter). It's a named directory -- works everywhere a path is expected, unlike
a cd-alias.

column1: Why use `hash -d name=~/dir` instead of `alias name='~/dir'` (or 'cd ~/dir')?
column2:
An alias that's JUST a path (alias notes='~/notes') doesn't cd -- the shell
tries to EXECUTE the directory (error). `hash -d` is the right tool:
- expands as a path fragment too:  ~work/sub/file  (a cd-alias can't)
- p10k/prompt collapses the real path to ~notes (short prompt)
- tab-completes after ~name
Gotcha: the form is ~name (tilde-prefixed). `cd notes` still fails; `cd ~notes`.
